title: Documenting NumPy Functions
keywords: errors, debugging, testing, and code quality
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of documenting numpy functions and name one situation where it is useful.
Apply describing inputs and outputs to a small NumPy example and inspect the resulting values, shape, or dtype.
Identify one important limitation, boundary case, or validation check for documenting numpy functions.

content.intro: This lesson develops topic 190 of the supplied curriculum: **Documenting NumPy Functions**. The main starting point is **Describing inputs and outputs**. You will connect the idea to a small, synthetic example, then use the result to reason about shape, dtype, accuracy, or memory as appropriate.
content.why_it_matters: Reliable numerical code makes failures reproducible and tests the invariants that matter: shape, dtype, finite values, exact results where appropriate, and tolerances for approximate results.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Treat **Documenting NumPy Functions** as an explicit step in an array workflow. This lesson centers on **Describing inputs and outputs** and the source syllabus's related subtopics. Before trusting a result, identify the input shape and dtype, perform the smallest useful operation, and inspect the output. The example uses synthetic data so you can change one value and observe what changes.

common_mistakes.problem: Testing approximate values with strict equality
common_mistakes.why: Numerical methods can legitimately introduce small rounding differences.
Empty inputs, invalid types, shape mismatch, and NaN may reveal defects.
common_mistakes.fix: Add explicit boundary and invalid-input tests.
